# shadow/hooks-in-owner

Require `use*` hooks to be created in a component or hook, not in loops, after early returns, or later.

`recommended`

## Why

Hooks such as `useEffect`, `onCleanup` and `useResource` attach to the owner that is current while a component or hook runs. Called at module level, from an event handler or a timer, they have no owner and are never disposed. Called in a loop they create unbounded computations, and called after an early `return` they are silently skipped for the branch that returned. Keep hooks at the top level of components and custom hooks, and use `<For>` for per-item state.

## Incorrect

```tsx
useEffect(() => track());
```

```tsx
function Page(props) {
  if (props.disabled) return <p />;
  const [n] = useSignal(0);
  return <b>{n}</b>;
}
```

```tsx
function List(props) {
  for (const item of props.items) useEffect(() => log(item));
  return <ul />;
}
```

```tsx
function Page() {
  return <button onClick={() => useEffect(run)} />;
}
```

## Correct

```tsx
function Page() {
  useEffect(() => track());
  return <p />;
}
```

```tsx
function useTimer() {
  onCleanup(stop);
}
```

```tsx
function Page(props) {
  const [n] = useSignal(0);
  return <Show when={!props.disabled}><b>{n}</b></Show>;
}
```

## Options

```json
[
  {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "additionalHooks": {
        "type": "array",
        "items": {
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "conditional": {
        "type": "boolean"
      }
    },
    "additionalProperties": false
  }
]
```

Defaults: `[{}]`

## Disabling

Disable one line with `// eslint-disable-next-line shadow/hooks-in-owner`, a block with `/* eslint-disable shadow/hooks-in-owner */` and `/* eslint-enable shadow/hooks-in-owner */`, or a whole file with the block form at its top. Disable it when the code supplies an owner the rule cannot see, for example a callback that a helper runs inside `createRoot` or `runWithOwner`.

## Notes

- `useSignal`, `useStore` and `useMemo` work without an owner, so only loops and early returns are reported for them.
- Option `conditional: true` (used by the strict config) also reports hooks inside `if`, `?:`, `&&` and `switch`.
- Option `additionalHooks` lists extra hook names (strings, matched exactly) that must follow the same rules.

## Messages

- `inLoop`: `{{name}}` is called inside a loop. Each iteration creates another owner-bound computation; use `<For>` / `<Index>` for per-item state, or move the hook out of the loop.
- `afterEarlyReturn`: `{{name}}` is called after an early return, so it is skipped for the branch that returned. Move it above the return, or use `<Show>`.
- `outsideOwner`: `{{name}}` needs an owner but runs {{where}}. Call it from a component or custom hook, or wrap the work in `createRoot` / `runWithOwner`.
- `conditional`: `{{name}}` is called conditionally. Create hooks unconditionally at the top level of the component or hook, and put the condition inside.

## Configs

| Config | Setting |
| --- | --- |
| `recommended` | warn |
| `strict` | error ({"conditional":true}) |
| `migration` | warn |
| `dusk` | warn |
